sense: a thing: no longer have it

terms.comment: First “let go”, and so to lose what one had, by mischance as much as by fault.

evidence: Vulg. Lc. 15.4: sī perdiderit ūnam ex illīs
terms.comment: To lose utterly, or throw away (operam perdere, to waste one’s effort); nōmen perdidī, I’ve forgotten the name. Its passive is pereō.

terms.grammar: verb, irregular, conjugated like eō: the passive of perdō
evidence: Vulg. Lc. 15.6: ovem meam, quae perierat
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: as the passive of perdō only pereō, perditus, perīre are in good use. So “it was lost” is perierat; in comedy Periī! is “I’m done for”.

phrases.english: Where did you lose the ball?

phrases.latin: ‘certē,’ inquit rīdēns, ‘nam nisi tū āmīsissēs, numquam recēpissem’
phrases.english: “Certainly,” he said with a smile, “for if you hadn’t lost it, I should never have taken it back.”
Oh no: I’ve forgotten the name.

phrases.latin: sī perdiderit ūnam ex illīs … Congrātulāminī mihi, quia invēnī ovem meam, quae perierat.
phrases.english: if he loses one of them … “Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep that was lost.”
